claims.claim: US 10-year constant-maturity yield, official daily curve
S&P Global flash US composite output index

stories.dek: The S&P 500 closed at 7,706.03, down 0.75%, with the Dow off 0.68% and the Nasdaq off 1.13%. The cause is the cost of government borrowing. After the close, the US Treasury published its official rate for the day: the ten-year yield at 5.11%, up from 4.96% on Tuesday. That is the biggest one-day jump this month and the highest reading since 2007. It followed a US business survey that came in far stronger than expected, which makes a rate cut less likely, not more. For someone holding good businesses for years, higher borrowing costs lower what future profits are worth today and squeeze anything that borrows. Watch Thursday's jobless claims at 13:30 UK.
stories.headline: Borrowing costs hit their highest since 2007 and shares fell
stories.short: Borrowing costs at a 2007 high; shares fell

stories.dek: The VIX, the market's fear gauge, closed at 15.18, up 6.83% on the day from 14.21, after ranging between 14.12 and 15.45. It has spent every session this week below 15. On the BuyTrigger ladder, under 15 is calm and 15 to 20 is normal, so the page now reads normal rather than calm. That is a change of label, not a change of weather: the system's buy window does not open until 30, and 15.18 is a long way from it. What it means for a long-term holder is simply that the market has started charging a little more for protection while borrowing costs reprice. Watch whether it holds above 15 on Thursday.
stories.headline: The fear gauge closed above 15 for the first time this week
stories.short: Fear gauge closes above 15, first time this week

claims.claim: One-day change in the 10-year (calculated from the two official readings)

stories.dek: For three editions today the US Treasury had not yet published its daily interest-rate table, so the only evidence was a live market quote. It has now posted: the ten-year rate at 5.11%, up from 4.96% on Tuesday, a jump of 15 basis points, or 0.15 of a percentage point, in a single day. The thirty-year went to 5.40% from 5.29% and the five-year to 4.99% from 4.83%. This is not the first time this month the official ten-year has been above 5% (18 September printed 5.01%), but it is the highest reading and the largest one-day move. It matters because this is the number mortgages, company debt and government borrowing are priced off. Thursday's table lands mid-afternoon UK time.
stories.headline: Official figures confirm the month's biggest jump in borrowing costs
stories.short: Official curve confirms the month's biggest rate jump

claims.claim: Gap between the Russell 2000 and the S&P 500 on the day (calculated)
Russell 2000 move at 20:36 UK, filed in the previous edition

stories.dek: The Russell 2000, the index of smaller US companies, closed down 1.77% against the S&P 500's 0.75% — a gap of 1.02 percentage points. Smaller companies carry more floating-rate debt and refinance more often, so they feel a rise in borrowing costs first and hardest. That pattern is the tell that separates a rate story from a growth scare: in a growth scare the damage usually starts with the economically sensitive giants instead. Two hours before the close the Russell was down only 1.55%, so the selling got worse into the bell rather than better. For a long-term holder this says the market is repricing the cost of money, not doubting that the economy is growing.
stories.headline: Smaller US companies had the worst day, which points at borrowing costs
stories.short: Smaller companies fell hardest, a borrowing-cost tell

claims.claim: Nasdaq Composite trailing the S&P 500 on the day (calculated from the two percentage moves)

stories.dek: Nvidia closed at $225.51, down 1.47%, and barely moved after hours. Two hours before the close I reported that technology shares were clawing back ground, with the Nasdaq trailing the S&P 500 by 0.35 percentage points. By the bell that gap had widened to 0.38 points, so the recovery faded instead of building. The reason is mechanical rather than about Nvidia's business: when the cost of borrowing rises, profits expected years from now are discounted harder, and the AI chain is the part of the market whose value sits furthest in the future. Nothing in today's move tells you anything about chip demand. The next real test is Micron's results on 30 September.
stories.headline: Nvidia ($NVDA) slipped and the late-day tech recovery did not hold
stories.short: Nvidia slips; the late tech recovery did not hold

claims.claim: WTI front-month crude, 16:59 ET electronic price (not the official settlement)
Brent front-month crude, 16:59 ET electronic price
Brent minus WTI (calculated from the two prices)

stories.dek: US crude ended the day at $92.71, up 2.42%, and Brent, the European benchmark, at $98.36, up 3.09%. Brent got within $1.22 of $100 at its high of $98.78 but did not reach it. The number worth watching is the gap between the two, which has now narrowed for a third session running, to $5.65 from $5.86 two hours earlier. Yesterday I read a widening gap as evidence the problem was confined to seaborne supply; a narrowing gap says the buying is in both American and European crude. Dearer oil feeds straight into the inflation figures that are pushing borrowing costs up. Watch whether Brent takes $100 on Thursday.
stories.headline: Oil closes near $93 as the gap with European crude keeps shrinking
stories.short: Oil near $93; gap with European crude keeps shrinking

claims.claim: Robinhood move at 20:36 UK, filed in the previous edition

stories.dek: Robinhood closed at $122.70, down 1.25%, and its closing price was effectively its worst of the session, with a day low of $122.28. That is a sharp change of character: two hours before the bell it was down only 0.24%, and for most of the day it had held up better than the market. I found no company announcement behind the move. A share that fades into the close on no news usually means sellers were working an order rather than reacting to anything, which tells you about today's trading and nothing about the business. After hours it was quiet. Watch for any filing overnight and how it opens on Thursday.
stories.headline: Robinhood ($HOOD) closed right on its low of the day
stories.short: Robinhood closes on its low after holding up all day

claims.claim: Edgewater Research note on slowing share gains, and Citi at Buy with a $600 target, as the cause of today's move
Date of the widely cited article on AppLovin price-target cuts

stories.dek: AppLovin closed at $315.25, down 4.10%, having traded as low as $304.77 before recovering about $10 into the bell. For three editions I reported that no firm had changed its rating on the company, which left a 4% fall with nothing attached to it. A named reason is now circulating — research from Edgewater suggesting the company's gains in market share may have slowed, with Citi still positive — but I could not date either item to today at a source I trust, and the widely shared article on price-target cuts turns out to be from 7 August. The price is confirmed; the cause is not. Watch for a dated note on Thursday.
stories.headline: AppLovin ($APP) fell 4% and a possible reason finally surfaced
stories.short: AppLovin down 4%; a possible reason surfaces, unconfirmed
